HOW TO USE
1. Use one fresh visit per profile; do not resume a different profile's saved information.
2. Send only the opening first. Use the answer bank as the chat asks; do not paste the whole profile.
3. There is no required question order. Rephrase naturally or use matching buttons.
4. Try the optional turn once at its stated moment. A correction supersedes the earlier answer.
5. For anything unspecified, say I don't know or leave it for later; do not invent facts.
6. All people, clinics, pharmacy names and Example medicines are fictional. These runs assess the UI and conversation, not real provider/drug matches.
7. All five retain ZIP 34102 from the original corpus so geography does not dominate the comparison between runs.

QUICK INDEX

M2: Jordan — helping a mother with existing coverage
M3: Denise — spouse's job coverage and a corrected end date

========================================================================
M1: Maya — retired beginner with COBRA
========================================================================
Recombined from: P2, P4-unknown, P7, P8

START BY SENDING
I'm 64 and retired last month. I want to get Medicare when I can, but I don't understand when that is.

ANSWER BANK — use only what the chat asks about
Who this is for:
This is for me.

Birthday:
I turn 65 in March 2027.

Current coverage:
I'm on COBRA. I don't have insurance from a current job.

Former job and work coverage:
My job and its active employee insurance ended October 31, 2026. COBRA started after that.

COBRA end:
The COBRA paperwork says April 30, 2027.

Medicare enrollment:
I haven't applied for Medicare and don't have Parts A or B.

Preferred start:
As soon as I'm eligible. I need help understanding the timing.

ZIP:
34102

Doctor:
Dr. Rivera at Example Clinic in Naples. That's the only doctor I want to keep.

Prescriptions:
Example Three. It's a tablet, but I don't know the strength.

Fill and pharmacy details:
I use Example Pharmacy in Naples, in person. I don't know the quantity or days supply right now.

Travel:
I only need routine care locally.

Priorities:
Lower monthly payments and keeping my doctor both matter. I haven't ranked them.

Learning preference:
I'm new to all of this. One small explanation at a time would help.

OPTIONAL TURN — try once
When: After the first explanation of the coverage paths
Send: Wait, is Medicare Advantage something I buy in addition to Original Medicare?
Notice: Does it resolve the confusion in plain language, then return naturally to the practical discussion?

UI POINTS TO WATCH
- Eligibility explanation arrives before a demand for a preferred date; COBRA stays distinct from current-job coverage.
- Unknown medicine strength stays open without trapping the chat or inventing a value.
- Doctor and medicine acknowledgments feel timely without recurring in every reply.

========================================================================
M2: Jordan — helping a mother with existing coverage
========================================================================
Recombined from: P3-replacement, P5, P9, P10

START BY SENDING
I'm helping my mom review her Medicare. She's happy with her doctors but wants to understand whether her coverage still makes sense.

ANSWER BANK — use only what the chat asks about
Who this is for:
My mother, Evelyn. She's 72. I'm helping her; this isn't about my coverage.

Current coverage:
She has Original Medicare, a Medigap policy and a separate Part D drug plan. She wants to keep them while she looks.

Actual enrollment:
She already has Parts A and B. Her Part B started in October 2020.

Desired timing:
No immediate change. We're reviewing what she already has.

ZIP:
Her ZIP is 34102.

Doctors:
Dr. Rivera at Example Clinic in Naples, and Dr. Lee at Example Hospital in Tampa.

Prescriptions:
She takes Example Med 5 mg tablets and Example Med 10 mg tablets. Please keep those as two separate entries.

5 mg fill:
For the 5 mg tablets: 30 tablets for 30 days, at Example Pharmacy in Naples, retail pickup.

10 mg fill:
For the 10 mg tablets: 60 tablets for 30 days, at Example Pharmacy in Naples, retail pickup.

Travel:
She needs routine care in Tampa and also spends summers in Ohio.

Priorities:
Keeping both doctors and more predictable costs matter most. She hasn't chosen one over the other.

Budget:
She'd like to keep premiums and what she spends on care to around $200 a month.

Helper's own coverage, only if relevant:
I have insurance through my current job. My mother doesn't have that insurance.

Learning preference:
Mom knows the basics, but I need a short explanation when unfamiliar terms come up.

OPTIONAL TURN — try once
When: After both medicine fills have been entered
Send: Correction: the 5 mg Example Med is filled as 90 tablets for 90 days. Keep the 10 mg prescription exactly as it was.
Notice: Does the correction affect only the named strength, without changing the other prescription or assigning the daughter's insurance to her mother?

UI POINTS TO WATCH
- The mother's reports stay separate from the helper's circumstances.
- Two strengths remain visually distinguishable and editable.
- Review and checklist content are readable without a large repeated profile recap in the conversation.

========================================================================
M3: Denise — spouse's job coverage and a corrected end date
========================================================================
Recombined from: P1, P1-payer, P6, P8

START BY SENDING
I turn 65 in December and my spouse is retiring soon. I'm trying to figure out what happens to my health insurance.

ANSWER BANK — use only what the chat asks about
Who this is for:
This is for me.

Birthday:
My 65th birthday is December 18, 2026.

Current coverage:
I'm insured through my spouse's current job. I'm not on COBRA.

Whose job ends:
My spouse's job ends December 15, 2026. It's not my job.

Initial insurance-end answer:
I think the insurance ends December 31, 2026.

Preferred start:
I'd prefer February 2027, but I want to understand how the timing works before deciding.

Actual Medicare enrollment:
I don't have Parts A or B and haven't applied yet.

Employer size:
My spouse's employer has about 60 employees.

HSA:
Yes, contributions are still going into my HSA.

ZIP:
34102

Doctors:
No particular doctors to include.

Prescription:
Example One, 10 mg tablet.

Fill:
30 tablets for 30 days, Example Pharmacy in Naples, retail pickup.

Travel:
I need routine care locally and in Tampa.

Priorities:
More predictable costs and flexibility when I'm in Tampa.

Learning preference:
I know a little about Medicare. Please keep the explanations brief unless I ask for more.

OPTIONAL TURN — try once
When: After the initial insurance end has been discussed
Send: I found the letter. Correction: my spouse retires December 15, 2026, but my insurance lasts through January 31, 2027. The job end date hasn't changed.
Notice: Does the chat update only the insurance end, preserve the job end and keep the February preference separate from a confirmed Medicare start?

UI POINTS TO WATCH
- Job end, insurance end and preferred Medicare start are easy to distinguish.
- The corrected date is reflected in any date summary and review.
- HSA and coverage questions have an understandable purpose without turning into a dense lecture.

========================================================================
M4: Sam — VA care, no prescriptions and a short explanation preference
========================================================================
Recombined from: P5, P7, P8, P4

START BY SENDING
I use the VA and turn 65 next year. Do I still need to look into Medicare?

ANSWER BANK — use only what the chat asks about
Who this is for:
This is for me.

Birthday:
I turn 65 in June 2027.

Military program:
VA care only. I don't have TRICARE or TRICARE for Life.

Coverage end:
I don't know of an end date for my VA care.

Actual Medicare enrollment:
I haven't applied and don't have Parts A or B.

Preferred start:
I don't know yet. I'd like to understand this first.

ZIP:
34102

Doctor, deliberately enter without an honorific:
Lee at Example Hospital in Tampa

Doctor clarification if asked:
That's Dr. Lee at Example Hospital in Tampa. I want to keep seeing that doctor.

Prescriptions:
I don't take any prescription medicines.

Travel:
I spend two months a year in Tampa and want routine care there too.

Priorities:
Keeping my doctor and understanding what I might pay each month.

Learning preference:
I'm a beginner, but shorter explanations work better for me.

OPTIONAL TURN — try once
When: After a longer explanation or when it asks for a preferred start again
Send: Can you make that simpler? I haven't picked a start month. Let's leave that open for now.
Notice: Does it shorten the explanation and leave the date open without inferring TRICARE coverage or repeating a no-medicines question?

UI POINTS TO WATCH
- VA is treated as the reported program, without silently becoming TRICARE.
- A bare doctor name can be acknowledged and clarified without an error or a repeated whole question.
- None and not-yet-decided answers move the conversation forward naturally.

========================================================================
M5: Avery — an existing Advantage member exploring a supplement
========================================================================
Recombined from: P3, P3-replacement, P4, P7

START BY SENDING
I'm already on Medicare Advantage, but I'd like to understand whether Original Medicare with a supplement would be different for me.

ANSWER BANK — use only what the chat asks about
Who this is for:
This is for me. I'm 68.

Current coverage:
My current coverage is Medicare Advantage. I'm keeping it while I learn about the alternatives.

Parts A and B:
I already have both Parts A and B. Part B started in October 2023.

Current Advantage episode:
This Medicare Advantage plan began January 2025.

Prior supplement:
I've never had a Medigap policy.

Desired timing:
I haven't chosen a change date. I want to understand the differences first.

ZIP:
34102

Doctors:
Dr. Rivera at Example Clinic in Naples.

Initial medicine list:
Example One 5 mg tablets and Example Two 10 mg capsules.

Example One fill:
30 tablets for 30 days, Example Pharmacy in Naples, retail pickup.

Example Two fill:
60 capsules for 30 days, Example Pharmacy in Naples, retail pickup.

Travel:
I'd like to be able to get routine care locally and during summers in Ohio.

Priorities:
More predictable bills and flexibility in where I get care. I don't want to rank those yet.

Income and assistance details:
I don't know whether I qualify for help with costs. I'd rather leave the financial details for later.

Learning preference:
I know some basics, but I don't understand what a supplement changes.

OPTIONAL TURN — try once
When: After the medicine list or fill details have been discussed
Send: Correction: Example One is a 10 mg tablet, not 5 mg. Example Two hasn't changed. Can we go back to the supplement question after that?
Notice: Does it update the right medicine, retain Example Two and return to the learning question without forcing a restart or implying a switch is approved?

UI POINTS TO WATCH
- A coverage-path explanation fits the question without promising that a switch or supplement is available.
- Medicine corrections remain understandable; old fill details are not presented as newly verified for the changed medicine.
- Unknown financial details do not dominate the conversation or block requested learning.
